newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-ING starts Brazil pulp-paper firms.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-ING starts Brazil pulp-paper firms.

text.p: -- ING Barings said it has begun coverage of Brazilian pulp and paper producers Aracruz Celulose S.A. and Industrias Klabin de Papel e Celulose S.A. with buy recommendations.

-- The Dutch investment bank also said in a report it was initiating coverage of three other paper-pulp firms -- Bahia Sul Celulose S.A., Ripasa S.A. and Cia Suzano de Papel e Celulose S.A. -- with sell ratings.
-- ING said Aracruz is expected to diversify its product and revenue base and gain access to new markets through its new shareholder, Anglo-American Corp.
-- It also said higher pulp prices and volume growth should increase Aracruz's operating margin from 17.3 percent in 1996 to 32.3 percent in 1997 and 49.3 percent in 1998.
-- It forecast Aracruz earnings at $121 million in 1997 and at $299 million with a free cash-flow of $293 million in 1998.

-- The bank said Klabin's will benefit from Brazil's economic growth because domestic sales account for 80 percent of its revenue. The firm is expanding in Mercosur and plans to build a new plant in Argentina.
-- "Significant earnings growth is expected for 1998, with a forecast of 165 million reais, up from 52 million reais forecast in 1997," it said.
-- Klabin also is expected to list American depositary receipts in 1997, which will boost the stock's liquidity.
-- Bahia Sul, a joint-venture between Suzano and Cia Vale do Rio Doce, is expected to continue reporting losses and negative free cash flow, despite recent debt restructuring.
-- "The stock is trading at 15 percent of book value but Bahia Sul is too risky to make it attractive," the report said.
-- Ripasa is expected to see operating losses improve to break-even in 1997 and a 39 million-real profit in 1998 but the firm needs a "more aggressive cost-cutting plan," it added.
-- Suzano may not have the financial strength to support its minority interests in Brazilian petrochemical firms, diversify as planned into telecoms and solve Bahia Sul's debt problems, it said.
-- It should see a small 19 million-real profit this year but any significant earnings in 1998 will be due solely to major contributions by affiliated paper producer Igaras, ING said.
